[1, 2] The 172-page complaint alleges that Amazon is a monopolist that leverages a series of interlocking anticompetitive and unfair strategies to unlawfully preserve its dominance. [2] According to the lawsuit, these actions stifle competitors and sellers from lowering prices, result in higher costs for consumers, and lead to a degradation in service quality for shoppers on the platform. [1, 2] <4> The Federal Trade Commission (FTC), along with 17 state attorneys general, filed a significant antitrust lawsuit against Amazon.com, Inc. on September 26, 2023. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, accuses the technology and online retail giant of being a monopolist that employs a series of interlocking anticompetitive and unfair strategies to illegally preserve its dominance. The complaint alleges that Amazon's conduct harms competition in two primary markets: the online superstore market serving shoppers and the market for online marketplace services for sellers. According to the FTC, Amazon's actions prevent rivals and sellers from offering lower prices, lead to degraded quality and service for shoppers, result in excessive fees for sellers, and stifle innovation, thereby preventing fair competition. The states of Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Nevada, New York, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin joined the FTC's lawsuit. The plaintiffs are requesting a permanent injunction to stop Amazon's unlawful practices and restore competition. A bench trial for the case is anticipated to begin in 2026. <5> On September 22, 2023, Amazon announced its plan to introduce limited advertisements to its Prime Video streaming service to allow for continued investment in content. Amazon stated that it aims to show 'meaningfully fewer ads than linear TV and other streaming TV providers.' The rollout is planned to extend to France, Italy, Spain, Mexico, and Australia later in 2024, with a further expansion to Brazil, India, Japan, the Netherlands, and New Zealand announced for 2025. <6> Amazon held its annual Devices and Services event on September 20, 2023, at its new headquarters in Arlington, Virginia. [23, 29] The event centered on the integration of generative AI into Amazon's services, most notably with the unveiling of a more conversational, AI-driven version of Alexa. [1, 8, 15] Key product announcements included the Echo Hub, a wall-mountable smart home control panel, an updated Echo Show 8 with a centered camera, and new Echo Frames smart glasses. [2, 22] Additionally, Amazon introduced the next-generation Fire TV Stick 4K and Fire TV Stick 4K Max, featuring Wi-Fi 6 and Wi-Fi 6E support respectively, alongside a new Fire TV Soundbar designed for immersive audio. [2, 22] <7> Amazon held its 'Prime Big Deal Days' sales event on October 10 and 11, 2023. This 48-hour global shopping event was exclusively for Amazon Prime members and was widely considered a second Prime Day for the year. The event, which served as a kickoff to the holiday shopping season, took place in 19 countries: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, the U.S., and the U.K. Amazon officially announced the specific dates for the event on September 18, 2023. This followed a more general announcement on August 8, 2023, that a sale called 'Prime Big Deal Days' would occur in October. <8> Amazon introduced a generative AI tool designed to help sellers create more engaging and detailed product listings. Announced at its annual seller conference, Accelerate 2023, the feature utilizes large language models (LLMs) to generate titles, bullet points, and full descriptions from just a few keywords or a brief summary provided by the seller. This innovation aims to simplify the listing creation process, allowing sellers to produce high-quality, consistent, and compelling content with significantly less effort. The models can infer product attributes, such as a table's shape from its diameter or a shirt's collar style from an image, to enrich the product information. While many sellers who tested the tool used the AI-generated content without revision, Amazon advises users to review all generated text for accuracy before publishing. <9> On August 1, 2023, Amazon announced the nationwide expansion of its virtual healthcare marketplace, Amazon Clinic, to all 50 U.S. states and Washington, D.C. This expansion added video visit capabilities nationwide to its existing message-based consultation service, which was available in 34 states. Initially launched in November 2022, Amazon Clinic connects adult patients aged 18-64 with licensed clinicians from third-party telehealth providers, including SteadyMD, Wheel, Curai Health, and Hello Alpha, for more than 30 common health concerns such as allergies, pink eye, and urinary tract infections. The service operates on a cash-pay basis, with costs displayed upfront, and does not accept insurance, though prescribed medications may be covered by a patient's insurance plan. Patients can access the service 24/7 through the Amazon website or mobile app without an appointment.

metadata.original_text: This time series records amazon data in the web search domain, with a collection frequency of weekly, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-07-07 to 2024-09-22. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Amazon's Project Kuiper, its satellite internet initiative, has opened a 172,000-square-foot satellite production facility in Kirkland, Washington. While the factory quietly began operations in April 2024, an official grand opening ceremony with U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell was held on June 27, 2024. [4, 6, 7] The facility, located near Project Kuiper's research and development headquarters in Redmond, is planned to eventually produce up to five satellites per day and will create more than 200 jobs. [5, 6, 7] The initial announcement of plans for the factory was made on October 27, 2022. [3, 5] The first production satellites are scheduled to ship from the facility in the summer of 2024, ahead of the first full-scale mission targeted for the fourth quarter of 2024. [2, 7] In conjunction with the facility, Amazon has partnered with the Lake Washington Institute of Technology to create a satellite technician certificate program to help build a skilled local workforce. [6] <2> Amazon's market capitalization surpassed $2 trillion for the first time on Wednesday, June 26, 2024, making it the fifth U.S. company to achieve this milestone. [2, 7] The company's stock rose nearly 4% to close at $193.61, pushing its market value to approximately $2.01 trillion. [4, 5, 6] This achievement was part of a broader, albeit modest, tech rally, with the Nasdaq Composite index also seeing gains. [1, 6] Amazon now joins the exclusive group of U.S. tech giants valued at over $2 trillion, which includes Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, and Alphabet. [6, 7] The surge in Amazon's valuation is largely attributed to investor optimism surrounding its advancements in artificial intelligence and the sustained growth of its cloud computing division, Amazon Web Services (AWS). [4] <3> Members of the Amazon Labor Union (ALU) at the JFK8 warehouse in Staten Island, New York, voted to affiliate with the 1.3 million-member International Brotherhood of Teamsters. [2] The vote, which took place on June 17, 2024, was 98.3% in favor of the affiliation, with a final tally of 829 votes for, 14 against, and 10 spoiled ballots. [3, 7] The affiliation establishes a new, chartered local, ALU-IBT Local 1, which will represent the approximately 5,500 workers at the JFK8 facility and has jurisdiction for Amazon warehouse workers across all five boroughs of New York City. [2, 6] This strategic partnership is intended to leverage the Teamsters' significant resources and power to pressure Amazon into negotiating a first contract, a process that has been stalled since the ALU's historic unionization win in 2022. [4, 5, 6] While the vote was overwhelmingly in favor, some outlets have noted the low turnout, with the 843 valid ballots representing a fraction of the total workforce at the warehouse. [3, 8] <4> On May 30, 2024, Amazon and Grubhub announced that a Grubhub+ membership would be a permanent, free perk for Amazon Prime members in the U.S. This ongoing benefit, valued at $120 a year, provides Prime members with $0 delivery fees on eligible orders over $12, reduced service fees, and 5% credit back on pickup orders. The partnership also integrated Grubhub's service directly into the Amazon.com website and the Amazon Shopping app, allowing customers to order from hundreds of thousands of restaurants without leaving the Amazon platform. This development made a previous promotional offer, which began in July 2022 as a one-year free trial, a lasting feature of the Prime membership. <5> In 2024, Amazon is undertaking a significant expansion of its U.S. logistics and distribution network after a two-year pause. [2] The company has leased, purchased, or announced plans for more than 16 million square feet of new warehouse space. [1, 2] This expansion is a key part of its strategic shift from a centralized national network to a regionalized model, designed to position goods closer to customers, thereby reducing delivery times and costs. [1] According to supply chain consulting firm MWPVL International, the 2024 plans include at least 170 new facilities in the U.S., comprising 103 package delivery stations and 21 small fulfillment centers. [1] This renewed investment in its physical infrastructure is aimed at supporting continued e-commerce growth and enhancing its capacity for rapid and same-day delivery. [1, 2] <6> At its inaugural Upfront presentation for advertisers in New York City on May 14, 2024, Amazon announced a robust slate of new and returning series for Prime Video. Among the major announcements was a series order for a live-action 'Tomb Raider' show, with Phoebe Waller-Bridge attached as writer and executive producer, though a lead actress has not yet been cast. The company also officially confirmed a live-action 'Spider-Man Noir' series, titled 'Noir,' starring Nicolas Cage as the aging 1930s private investigator and superhero. Additionally, Amazon revealed that a sequel to the 'Road House' remake is in development, with Jake Gyllenhaal set to return to his role; the first film has become Prime Video's most-watched original movie debut, with nearly 80 million viewers. The presentation also included renewal announcements for returning shows. 'Mr. & Mrs. Smith' was renewed for a second season, though it is not expected that stars Donald Glover and Maya Erskine will return, suggesting a potential anthology format for the series. While 'Reacher' was mentioned as a returning hit show, its third season renewal had been confirmed prior to the event, with filming already underway. <7> On April 25, 2024, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced its plan to invest $11 billion to construct a new data center campus in St. Joseph County, Indiana. [1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8] This project, located near New Carlisle, represents the largest single capital investment in Indiana's history and is expected to create at least 1,000 new jobs. [1, 2, 7] The new data centers will house servers, storage, and networking equipment to power cloud computing and generative AI technologies. [1, 2] As part of the investment, AWS will also contribute up to $7 million for local road infrastructure improvements. [3, 7] The state of Indiana is supporting the project with a package of performance-based incentives and tax exemptions. [2, 7, 9]
